resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Tuples[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

[b]Tuples [/b]are very similar to lists, except that they are immutable (they cannot be changed). 
Also, they are created using [b]parentheses[/b], rather than square brackets.

[s0l0!-header][b]Example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" ]words = [b]([/b]"spam", "eggs", "sausages"[b])[/b][/code]
You can access the values in the tuple with their index, just as you did with lists:[code format="py" codeId="365"]print(words[0])[/code]
Trying to reassign a value in a tuple causes an error. [code format="py" codeId="366"]words[1] = "cheese"[/code]
[note]Like lists and dictionaries, tuples can be nested within each other.[/note]

填空，期望程序依次生成列表，字典，元组。

```typein
# 列表
list = __0__"one", "two"__1__

# 字典 
dict = __2__1:"one", 2:"two"__3__

# 元组 
tp = __4__"one", "two"__5__
```

resolved.title: 元组
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Tuples[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

An advantage of tuples over lists is that they can be used as keys for dictionaries (because they are immutable):[code format="py" codeId="3123"]dict = {
    ("David", 42): "red",
    ("Bob", 24): "green"
}

print(dict[("Bob", 24)]) [/code]
[note]Tuples are faster than lists, but they cannot be changed.[/note]
